get.summary: Everything the comparison page needs in one call: run, model, per-site horizon, series, windows, metrics, criteria
get.description: Defaults: default run, every site of the run, the whole run range, data step (3600 s), max_points 10000, horizon_step_deg 1, criteria_hours 24,72,168, include horizon,series,windows,metrics,criteria (opt-in: pointing -> sites[].now = where to point the panel and the antenna at range.start, as GET /sites/{site_id}/pointing; survival_hint -> sites[].survival_hint = longest dark period + the battery a reference night_load_w needs; their assumptions are in `assumptions`). metrics also carry energy proxies mean_power_tracking_pct / mean_power_horizontal_pct over the range. Series are decimated per site to <= max_points while keeping both samples around every visibility transition (see DatasetSeries). Windows / metrics / criteria are computed from the full-resolution windows over the requested range (whole run -> exactly summary.csv / windows.json). Payload limit: the series points of all sites together (regular + transition samples, exactly as returned) must be <= 50000 (about 4.5 MB of JSON, ~1 MB gzip), else 422 OUT_OF_RANGE (title "Series point limit exceeded") with the numbers and a fitting max_points; first check (before any read): sites x min(max_points, n_samples / k) - so a call with no parameters on a 23-site 5-year run is 422; e.g. all 23 sites x 31 days hourly = 17 112 points is fine, the whole 5-year run for many sites needs max_points <= 50000 / n_sites or fewer site_ids (a large step_s alone may not be enough: transition samples are always kept). Windows and horizon bytes are not counted. Without `series` in include there is no point limit (whole run, 23 sites: ~0.7 MB, ~0.2 s); a whole-run series for all sites takes ~8 s, so request series for <= 1 year or a few sites. A range partly outside the run is clamped (coverage = partial); no overlap -> 422 OUT_OF_RANGE. Unknown site id -> 404 SITE_NOT_FOUND.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Run to read; default = the run flagged is_default (GET /api/v1/runs)

parameters.name: site_ids
parameters.description: Comma separated site ids (max 100, duplicates ignored, response keeps this order). Default: every site of the run in sites.json order.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Inclusive start (default: run start). Snapped DOWN to the sample grid.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: EXCLUSIVE end (default: run end). Snapped UP to the sample grid. A range partly outside the run is clamped (coverage = partial); no overlap -> 422 OUT_OF_RANGE.

parameters.name: step_s
parameters.description: Desired spacing of the series, seconds (default = the data step, 3600). The server keeps every k-th sample, k = floor(step_s / data step), PLUS both samples around every Sun/Earth visibility transition, and raises k further if needed so a site never exceeds max_points. The spacing actually used is series.step_s.

parameters.name: max_points
parameters.description: Cap on series points per site (default and max 10000), transition samples included. Also: the series points of all sites together must be <= 50000, else 422 OUT_OF_RANGE with title "Series point limit exceeded".

parameters.name: horizon_step_deg
parameters.description: Azimuth step of the returned horizon curve: 1 (default, 361 points 0..360) or 0.5 (721 points, ~4 KB per site). The stored silhouette is 0.5 deg for most sites: 1 POINT-SAMPLES it at whole degrees (the half-degree samples are dropped, so a narrow peak between two whole degrees is not drawn and a Sun / Earth marker can appear on the wrong side of the drawn curve near it). Only 0.5 is exactly consistent with sun_visible / earth_visible; prefer it for rim sites (or all sites) when drawing markers against the horizon.

parameters.name: criteria_hours
parameters.description: Comma separated minimum durations in hours (> 0, max 30; deduplicated and sorted ascending). Each one is evaluated against longest_both_h.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma separated parts of each site to return: horizon, series, windows, metrics, criteria, pointing, survival_hint (default: horizon,series,windows,metrics,criteria; pointing and survival_hint are opt-in). Omitted parts are absent from sites[]. pointing -> sites[].now = where to point the solar panel and the antenna at range.start (same block as GET /sites/{site_id}/pointing); survival_hint -> sites[].survival_hint = the longest dark period of the range and the battery a night_load_w load needs to bridge it.

parameters.name: night_load_w
parameters.description: Reference load while the Sun is hidden, W, >= 0 (as POST /mission/survival night_load_w; include=survival_hint): survival_hint.required_battery_wh = the battery this load needs to bridge the longest dark period of the range (null when omitted). Ignored without survival_hint. For a real panel and day load use POST /mission/survival.

post.summary: Start a Python job (async): custom_site, precompute, analyse, alt_dates_python, check, validate, ...
post.description: Body = CreateJobRequest, discriminated on `type` (one schema per job type; GET /api/v1/capabilities lists the types this server runs - others answer 501 JOB_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE). 202 = queued, or an identical job is already queued/running: you are then subscribed to it (cached: true, same job_id; poll `poll` every 1-2 s; `Location` header = the same URL). 200 = an identical job already succeeded (cached: true). 429 TOO_MANY_JOBS when this client (IP) already waits on JOB_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_CLIENT (default 2) queued/running jobs; 429 QUEUE_FULL when JOB_QUEUE_MAX jobs wait. Job types that import a run (custom_site, precompute) have a storage budget: 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED beyond JOB_RUNS_MAX_PER_CLIENT live runs of this client, 503 STORAGE_FULL when the server keeps JOB_RUNS_MAX_TOTAL runs / JOB_RUNS_MAX_MB or DATA_DIR is low on space; dem pgda work: 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED once the daily PGDA download budget is used. 409 RUN_NOT_READY when a run the job reads (check, compare_runs, ...) is still importing or failed. start snaps down / end snaps up to whole hours. When succeeded, use result.run_id with the normal endpoints. Measured on the dev machine (1 site, hourly, spice + pgda + raymarch, PGDA tiles of the area already cached): POST -> succeeded in ~14 s for 1 month and ~19 s for 1 year (precompute 11-18 s, import 1-3 s). The first job in a polar area not yet cached also downloads PGDA tiles and can take minutes.

DatasetSeries.description: Columnar series (all arrays have the same length, <= max_points). Decimation keeps sample 0, every k-th sample, the last sample, and the samples i-1 and i around every change of sun_visible or earth_visible, so a rise or set is never lost (exact to +- one data step). When decimated, t is IRREGULAR (transition samples sit between the regular ones): plot by timestamp. The last sample is range.end - range.step_s (end is exclusive). Use the *_visible flags (or windows) for visibility: they are NOT el > 0 (Sun upper limb, Earth centre + clearance, terrain horizon, mast height).

source.description: Literature / catalog source of the coordinates

height_m_input.description: null = surface height read from the DEM

observer_height_m.description: Mast height above the surface, m

SiteRecord.description: sites.json record of the run (docs/OUTPUT_SPEC.md 3.2), without file paths

run_id.description: Run id: `pf_<params_fingerprint>` for imported precompute runs, `job_<job_id>` for custom jobs

step_s.description: Sample step of the run, seconds

precision_h.description: = step_s / 3600. Every boundary and "hours until" value is accurate to +- this many hours.

site_id.description: Site id: catalog id (`a3_haworth`) or canonical custom id (`custom:-89.4500:222.6900`). Contains ":" -> always encodeURIComponent() it in paths.

sample_utc.description: Start of the sample that was read (<= t)

sample_index.description: k = floor((t - run start) / step_s). Always present in real responses.

hours_until.description: The precomputed hours_until_* columns of sample k = lunarnav.windows.hours_until_state(...)[k]: hours from sample_utc (+- precision_h); 0 = already in that state; null = no such event before run end

next_events.description: Same events measured from t itself (Python NextEvent semantics, incl. lower_bound). Always present in real responses.

hours.description: Hours from t (the requested instant, NOT sample_utc) until the event; 0 = condition already holds

at.description: Instant of the event (= t when it already holds); null when it does not happen before the run end

lower_bound.description: true -> no event before the run end: hours = time to the run end (a lower bound)

run_id.description: Run id: `pf_<params_fingerprint>` for imported precompute runs, `job_<job_id>` for custom jobs

kind.description: precompute = imported Colab output; custom = result of a POST /jobs

is_default.description: Used when a request omits run_id

expires_at.description: custom runs are deleted after this instant; null = kept

params_fingerprint.description: 16-hex hash of the computation parameters (lunarnav manifest)

code_version.description: lunarnav version that produced the run

provider.description: Ephemeris method: horizons | spice | analytic | synthetic

step_s.description: Sample step of the run, seconds

items.description: Site id: catalog id (`a3_haworth`) or canonical custom id (`custom:-89.4500:222.6900`). Contains ":" -> always encodeURIComponent() it in paths.

anyOf.description: Run id: `pf_<params_fingerprint>` for imported precompute runs, `job_<job_id>` for custom jobs

default_run_id.description: Run used when a request omits run_id (null = nothing imported yet)

total.description: Number of runs matching the filters (all pages)

runs.description: This page: default run first, then most recently imported first
